## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Use Xiao’s kernel with at most (d³+4d²+5d+3)k vertices and reduced budget at most k.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_d(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O_d(k^{d+2}+k)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $\max\{d+2,3\}$ |

## Derivation

1. For each kernel vertex v and each set S of d+1 distinct neighbors of v, add $x_v\vee\bigvee_{u\in S}x_u$.

2. These clauses say that no retained vertex has d+1 retained neighbors. Add the linear-size cardinality encoding.

3. There are O_d(k) variables and polynomially many clauses of fixed width max(d+2,3). Apply the general-density SAT assumption directly at that width.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- d is fixed, not an additional input parameter hidden in the polynomial exponent.
- Do not convert every width-(d+2) clause to 3-CNF: that can introduce too many variables.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
